# Quality of the measurement {#sec-quality}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../_setup.R")
sc <- synth_counts(n_per_group = 4)
depth <- data.frame(sample = colnames(sc$counts), group = sc$samples$group,
                    reads = colSums(sc$counts))
min_count <- report_param("min_count")
kept <- rowMeans(sc$counts) >= min_count
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## In plain terms
This chapter checks whether each sample was measured well enough to use, and how many features had enough signal to analyse.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Status
Last run on the synthetic example data, `r format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d")`. Replace with your data source and date.
:::

**Question.** Is every sample measured deeply enough, and how many features pass the count filter?

**Design.** All `r fmt(nrow(depth))` samples are described. Nothing is tested.

Depth is the total count per sample. A feature is kept when its mean count across all samples is at least `r min_count`.

## Depth per sample {#sec-quality-depth}

Example output on synthetic data. Replace with your analysis.

```{r}
#| label: fig-quality-depth
#| fig-cap: "Total counts per sample for the synthetic example, one bar per sample, filled by group. The dashed line marks the median depth across all samples."
#| fig-alt: "A bar chart of total counts for six samples. Bars for the control and treated groups have similar heights around the dashed median line."
ggplot(depth, aes(sample, reads, fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(depth$reads), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(OKABE_ITO[1:2])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Total counts", fill = "Group")
```

The lowest depth was `r fmt(min(depth$reads))` and the highest was `r fmt(max(depth$reads))`, a ratio of `r round(max(depth$reads) / min(depth$reads), 2)`.

<!-- Q
- Which sample has the lowest depth, and is it below any stated cut-off?
- Does depth differ between groups?
-->

## Features kept {#sec-quality-filter}

Of `r fmt(length(kept))` features, `r frac(sum(kept), length(kept))` passed the mean-count filter of `r min_count`.

<!-- Q
- How many features were removed by the filter, and from which part of the count range?
-->

Limitations from this chapter are gathered in @sec-limitations.
